    Mailing list

    Get the reports by email

    Put your name on the list and Sean sends you the board's reports by hand after each session — the Morning Briefing PDF every trading day, the Evening Court, and the weekend Week in Review and Week Ahead. Research reports from an AI boardroom, never advice; name and email only; leave any time.

    You do not have to run the app to read what the board writes. Put your name on the list below and Sean sends the reports the app generates on his own machine — as PDFs, by ordinary email, by hand, after each session. The list is small and personal: it exists so a few people can follow an AI boardroom argue with itself and be graded on it, not to sell anyone anything.

    What you get#

    Each trading day · morning

    The Morning Briefing#

    The PDF the app builds after the 7:00 ET session: the Executive's memo and house rules, the market context, and the twenty leads — ten option leads and ten stock leads — each with entry, live price, stop, target, a time horizon and a read-across.

    What is in it

    Each trading day · evening

    The Evening Court#

    After the close: the day scored against the tape, every seat's on base / off base and its lesson, the Pyramid re-formed, and what the court changed for tomorrow. The board grading the board.

    What is in it

    Saturday · Sunday

    The weekend pair#

    Saturday morning the Week in Review — the just-ended week scored; Sunday evening the Week Ahead — a prospectus for the coming one. Month and year editions when a period ends.

    What is in them

    When they arrive#

    After each session, sent by Sean by hand. The app drafts the message and attaches the day's PDF; he reads it and clicks Send — so expect the Morning Briefing mid-morning rather than on the dot of 7:00, the Evening Court later in the evening, and the weekend pair on Saturday and Sunday. Nothing is sent automatically, by a schedule or a robot. Some days there is no report at all (a market holiday, a machine that was asleep — the app's schedule only runs while it is open); no report means no email, never a filler.

    What it is not#

    Research reports from an AI boardroom — not advice

    Every report is model output: sixteen personas on a language model reading public data, grading it, and scoring themselves against the close. They are frequently wrong, never personalised — the list does not know your finances, your horizon or your tolerance for loss, and everyone receives the same PDF — and not reviewed by any licensed professional. Nothing in them is a recommendation to buy or sell anything, and no email from this list will ever ask you for money or tell you what to do with yours. Options can expire worthless. The full statement is on Not financial advice.

    Privacy#

    • Name and email only, plus the two preferences you tick below (how you trade, which reports). Never sold, never shared, never used for anything but sending you these reports. The emails carry no tracking pixels.
    • The list lives in a small Firebase (Google Cloud) database that only Sean can read. A web browser can only add a record — never read, change or delete one — and the app pulls the list onto his own machine when he clicks Sync.
    • Leave any time: reply STOP to any report, or use the unsubscribe page. Either is honoured at the next sync, before the next send.

    How the list works#

    For the curious, and for the record. The form above writes one document straight from your browser to a Firestore collection called subscribers — there is no server in between. The document's id is the SHA-256 of your lowercased address, so the same address can only be on the list once, and the database rules allow create only: no browser, including yours, can read, change or delete a record. When the database is not configured (the Firebase project is not set up yet, the single-file edition, or no network) the page says so and the button becomes Subscribe by email, opening your own mail app with the request prefilled.

    On the other end the list is a tab in the app: Sean clicks Sync to pull new sign-ups and unsubscribe requests onto his machine, the app drafts the day's message with the right PDF attached, and he reads it and clicks Send — one batch of blind-copied recipients at a time, from his own mail account, after a dry run he can see. Every email ends with the research-tool footer, a STOP line and a link to the unsubscribe page, which writes to a second create-only collection, unsubscribe_requests, that the next sync honours. There is no scheduler, no automation and no service: if he does not click, nothing goes out.
